evals.prompt: Help me start an adapted Evo 2 phage-design project. I have not chosen the exact target, objective, SFT run, or execution settings, but I can answer questions.
evals.expected_output: A concise interactive intake that resolves the biologically material choices before execution.
assertions: The response identifies target, host, intended use, outcome, whole-genome scope, evidence needs, and success criteria.
It makes a provisional therapeutic assumption visible when intended use is unspecified.
It asks only questions whose answers materially change the experiment and can inspect available evidence or prior results first.
It defaults to complete genomes and does not infer an RBP-only or locus-only task.
For a new 7B project it selects evo2/7b-1m:1.0 with model size evo2_7b, while treating a checkpoint-family change in an existing run as a new attempt.
It creates a compact project summary and RUNLOG.md rather than a large process framework.

evals.prompt: Plan a PhiX174 paper replication locally on eight H100s. Prevent cluster leakage and keep it progressing after approval while I am offline.
evals.expected_output: A science-first end-to-end plan with durable execution and evidence-based checkpoint selection.
assertions: The response collects and validates full genomes, uses cluster-held-out splits, and keeps the target prompting neighborhood in training when required.
It sizes context and SFT duration from the actual corpus and selects checkpoints from validation rather than copying a paper step.
It calibrates sampling from the selected SFT serialization and keeps calibration, RL validation, and final rollout separate.
Before RL, it prepares and records a model-only, optimizer-free, runtime-sanitized SFT checkpoint while retaining the original full-state SFT checkpoint for SFT resume.
It uses a worker and monitoring facility that survives the chat process and can be reattached by job identifier.
It respects stage dependencies while overlapping independent evidence, preparation, or objective work when resources and write scopes permit.

It treats the example launcher as a reference implementation that may be run, adapted, wrapped, or replaced, using the README, stage subskills, and dependency DAG without prescribing one orchestration.
It runs every enabled reward and QC component with positive and failure controls and records useful progress in RUNLOG.md.
It generates and screens the requested full genomes and reports the final denominator and limitations.

evals.prompt: Plan therapeutic phage designs for productive infection of a new resistant bacterial strain. A receptor-binding module looks important, but I did not authorize a regional edit or fixed backbone.
evals.expected_output: A whole-genome lifecycle plan that treats host prediction as one signal.
assertions: The response defaults output and mutable scope to complete genomes and asks before any material scope reduction.
It covers adsorption and entry, defense and counter-defense, replication, morphogenesis and packaging, lysis and progeny, viable-reference support, and intended-use safety.
It defines the desired host direction, including target gain and any original-host retention or off-target avoidance.
It does not treat similarity as an edit mask or a host-model score as proof of productive infection.
It keeps computational objectives, final hard QC, and experimental validation distinct.

evals.prompt: How would you make a small, single-user computational phage-generation pilot scientifically reproducible, and decide whether it is ready to scale?
evals.expected_output: An electronic-lab-notebook reproducibility plan centered on the scientific experiment rather than software supply-chain ceremony.
assertions: The response records the biological question, input dataset and target, model checkpoint, key settings, random seeds, tool and data versions that affect interpretation, commands, outputs, and observed results.
It uses a concise RUNLOG.md and summary so another computational scientist can understand and repeat the pilot.
It includes positive and failure controls, denominators, and known limitations.

Most detail goes to experimental design, controls, outcomes, and limitations; the response does not make file or tree hashes, immutable source snapshots, clean-checkout rituals, or Git-state audits prerequisites for this single-user pilot.

evals.prompt: Plan an adapted whole-genome phage product with a biological endpoint that the recipe's existing rewards only partially describe. Two tested reward implementations are relevant but neither captures the complete goal. Decide how to construct the RL portfolio.
evals.expected_output: A portfolio that reuses sound tested machinery while inventing the target-specific scores needed to express the requested product.
assertions: The response identifies translating the desired final product into complementary measurable RL scores as a core agentic task.
It prefers modifying tested reward implementations when their measurements and failure semantics genuinely fit the new goal instead of rewriting them needlessly.
Because this is beyond a faithful experiment rerun, it expects to invent novel terminal or intermediate reward functions for important aspects not captured by the existing portfolio.
New scores are creatively grounded in relevant literature, biological reasoning, viable references, domain tools, and prior or partial-run evidence rather than forced from an ill-fitting proxy.
Each new or modified score has a documented endpoint relationship, zero and target anchors, calibrated partial credit, controls, telemetry, missing or failure behavior, and final-QC role.
It preserves component-level interpretability and versions the objective set as evidence changes.
